newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro shares ease ahead of U.S. jobs figures.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro shares ease ahead of U.S. jobs figures.

text.p: European shares took a few steps backwards in early business on Friday when the enthusiasm which drove them to new records in the previous day's trading was tempered by caution ahead of a crucial set of U.S. jobs figures.
"We're not going to move out of a fairly narrow range ahead of the data," a share dealer in London said. "It's the big number of the week and it has got some people worried."

Analysts say a stronger than expected rise in U.S. jobs during February could indicate the world's leading economy was overheating and lead to higher interest rates to choke off the threat of inflation.
Higher interest rates would be bad news for share prices by making the cost of borrowing more expensive for companies and alternative investments more attractive to investors.
Any selloff in U.S. share prices, which are at record levels, would undermine European share prices, too.
Economists' forecasts for the increase in U.S. jobs, due out at 1330 GMT, range from 118,000 to 260,000 with the average around 230,000.

London's FTSE 100 index crept into record territory at the start of trade but share prices were mixed and dealers said that nervousness ahead of the U.S. jobs figures would prevent the market charging upwards.

The FTSE was up just 0.3 of a point at 4,399.6, edging ahead despite Wall Street's retreat from its early gains on Thursday, when the Dow ended 1.15 points lower having been up 35 points when London closed.
But declining stocks outnumbered gainers in the FTSE and dealers said the market's marginal advance was led by a handful of shares, with Glaxo Wellcome Plc, BTR Plc and GKN Plc in the vanguard.

Positive newspaper comment about a bundle of blue-chip annual results released on Thursday, particulalry those of Glaxo, should help keep the downside limited, traders said. The continued liquidity of the market is also seen helping support shares.
"All the institutions still seem to be awash with cash and obviously that will be a positive factor," one dealer said.
But he added that the market's rise to record heights might prompt some nervousness and profit-taking, saying: "Some people seem to feel slightly giddy up here."

In Paris, profit-taking took French shares lower at the opening, after sharp gains in the last few days and Thursday's 1.23 percent rise, traders said. Wall Street's weak close also contributed to the easing.

But the market was well supported, with non-resident investors still finding Paris attractive. "They are forced to come in, the market is going up," said one trader. Company earnings were considered good, particularly those of Promodes.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 8.47 at 2,690.45 at 1000 GMT.
Germany's 30-share blue-chip DAX index kicked off bourse trading sharply lower with traders in Frankfurt seeking inspiration to give direction and cure a hangover from the record run of recent days.
The DAX index fell below the 3,400-point level early on and stood at 3,380.47 points, down 37.13 points, or 1.09 percent.
"There isn't very much going on this morning and we don't expect to go back over 3,400 points while we are waiting for U.S. data this afternoon," said a Frankfurt trader.
In currencies, the dollar was slightly firmer against the mark in early European trade but then eased back with the market focusing on the U.S. jobs figures.

Analysts said dollar/mark was likely to remain in a tight range below Thursday's 34-month high at 1.7210 as traders await what is expected to be a strong number. The dollar was trading at 1.7127 marks.

"I think it will be a strong number -- all the anecdotal evidence points that way -- and that could see the dollar make new highs above 1.7230 and maybe even 1.73," said Lee Ferridge, foreign exchange strategist at Commerzbank in London.

Some analysts said the potential positive news from the U.S. employment report might already be factored into the currency market. They see the possibility of profit-taking after the report unless the rise in payrolls exceeds expectations, given that it has been a strong week for the dollar. Hourly earnings data will also be watched closely for any sign of inflationary pressure.
Dollar/yen, meanwhile, was weighed down by comments from U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin on Thursday saying a sustained current account surplus by Japan "was in nobody's interest".
The yen has also been buoyed by continued talk of repatriation of Japanese funds ahead of Japanese fiscal year-end on March 31.
The lira strengthened further overnight and tested its mid-rate in the European exchange rate mechanism at 990 per mark.
CURRENCIES AT 1000 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7127 marks and 121.27 yen, compared with 1.7168 marks and 121.20 yen late on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1000 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 0.3 of a point at 4,399.6.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 8.47 points at 2,690.45.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 37.13 points at 3,380.47.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1000 GMT
Gold was fixed at $351.70 compared with London's close on Thursday of $352.20.
